NFV Refutation Review

Historical refutations and author feedback. Expand a row for evidence or click a comment to review it.

Interpretation and saving feedback

A counterexample to a generated model is not necessarily a Z3 bug. These preliminary assessments question specific witnesses; they do not prove the C++ correct.

Feedback is backed by version-controlled review JSON in Z3Prover/bench. Automatic imports never overwrite it. Author OK means agreement with the assessment, not verification of a fix. Submit several changed rows together through one prefilled GitHub issue; automation saves them in one commit after checking your Bench write permission. Submitted comments will be public on this page.

Initial assessments are source/report inspection, not independently replayed NFV proofs. Linked issue/PR status is recorded at review time, not checked live.

seq.eq recognizer reads arguments without checking arity Possible bug Z3Prover/z3#10958 - issue filed OK

seq.eq recognizer reads arguments without checking arity

eq_recognizer_requires_binary_marker
manual-seq-skolem-20260927T191033Z · skolem::is_eq
src/ast/seq/seq_skolem.cpp (Reviewed location)

Assessment and caveats

The family/symbol predicate does not require binary arity before argument reads. The generic internal constructor accepts nonbinary markers, while the dedicated mk_eq constructor creates binary ones. This is an internal robustness concern; no path from ordinary SMT-LIB input or wrong solver answer has been established.

Source inspected: d799f787d6fc9c16eb4a3ebbe63e6593e9b23a98

Reported model evidence

Assumption
e is any well-formed expression; result.a and result.b denote the output-reference values after the call.
Asserted claim
result == (is_seq_skolem_app(e) && skolem_symbol(e) == "seq.eq" && num_args(e) == 2) && (result => result.a == arg(e,0) && result.b == arg(e,1))
Reported witness
is_seq_skolem_app(e) && skolem_symbol(e) == "seq.eq" && num_args(e) == 0

HNF gather contract may not match the private helper's caller invariant Needs investigation — Pending

HNF gather contract may not match the private helper's caller invariant

create_b_gathers_requested_basis_rows
manual-hnf-cutter-20260927T163447Z · hnf_cutter::create_b
src/math/lp/hnf_cutter.cpp (Reviewed location)

Assessment and caveats

The witness uses duplicate basis rows [0,0], but the caller produces distinct pivot-row indices. In the full-rank case it keeps the matrix and RHS together in original order. Always permuting the RHS may be wrong for that caller. This is a preliminary contract-mismatch assessment, not a proof that every reachable input is safe; confirm the producer/caller invariant before proposing a fix.

Source inspected: d799f787d6fc9c16eb4a3ebbe63e6593e9b23a98

Reported model evidence

Assumption
forall k < basis_rows.size(): basis_rows[k] < m_right_sides.size()
Asserted claim
result.size() == basis_rows.size() && forall k < result.size(): result[k] == m_right_sides[basis_rows[k]]
Reported witness
basis_rows == [0, 0]; |m_right_sides| == 2; m_right_sides[0] != m_right_sides[1]

Empty-refinement schedule claim needs a finishing-helper frame contract Needs investigation — Comment

Empty-refinement schedule claim needs a finishing-helper frame contract

empty_refinement_still_checks_transcendentals
manual-nla-core-20260927T163619Z · core::on_to_refine_empty
src/math/lp/nla_core.cpp (Reviewed location)

Assessment and caveats

The postulated finishing helper arbitrarily replaces the schedule after the notification. The real wrapper does notify the schedule and return the finishing result. The counterexample exposes an unconstrained helper effect, but inspection of the wrapper alone does not prove what the actual helper preserves. Further helper/frame-contract analysis is needed.

Source inspected: d799f787d6fc9c16eb4a3ebbe63e6593e9b23a98

Reported model evidence

Assumption
m_to_refine is empty on entry; Finish(S) denotes the return and post-state of check_transcendentals_and_finish() from state S.
Asserted claim
result.squeeze_schedule == OnNothingToRefine(pre.m_squeeze_schedule) && result.return == Finish(state_after_schedule_notification).return && result.state_after_finish == Finish(state_after_schedule_notification).state
Reported witness
m_to_refine == []; pre == CoreState(SqueezeSchedule(0), 0); finishEnvironment == ((s: CoreState) => FinishResult(l_true, CoreState(SqueezeSchedule(1), 0)))

optional_witness_materialization
Z3Prover/z3#10764 · view_witness::materialize_witness
src/ast/seq/seq_view_witness.cpp (Reviewed location)

Assessment and caveats

The exact NFV witness uses an asserted non-sequence expression after a successful check, which the real check does not permit. A related sequence-sorted backtracking case was investigated in the linked PR. That PR was closed without merging: this is already reported, not a confirmed landed fix.

Reported model evidence

Assumption
m_enable_witness is true, m_last_result is l_true, stored witnesses were produced by a semantically correct successful check, and x is a live expression.
Asserted claim
(exists(a in m_assertions, a.var == x) -> !is_null(result) && forall(a in m_assertions, a.var == x, view_accepts(a.view, denote_seq(result)))) && (!exists(a in m_assertions, a.var == x) && is_sequence_sort(x.sort) -> denote_seq(result) == []) && (!exists(a in m_assertions, a.var == x) && !is_sequence_sort(x.sort) -> is_null(result))
Reported witness
m == Manager(0); x == OtherExpr(Manager(0), 0, BasicSort(Manager(0), 0)); m_witnesses == WitnessMap(map[]); m_assertions == [MaterializationAssertion(x, View(0))]

NFV report · Audit / report · Z3Prover/z3#10802 - closed, not merged

Link to this finding

Saved author input: Comment

This is code smell expr_ref view_witness::materialize_witness(expr* x) { expr_ref result(m); if (!m_enable_witness || m_last_result != l_true) return result; expr* witness = nullptr; if (m_witnesses.find(x, witness)) return expr_ref(witness, m); sort* elem_sort = nullptr; if (u().is_seq(x->get_sort(), elem_sort)) result = u().str.mk_empty(x->get_sort()); return result; } The type check for x should have been a pre-condition, not a defensive check added late in the code path. It is actionable

ebits >= 2; sbits >= 2; int_expr denotes an arbitrary mathematical integer x; rm is one of RNE, RNA, RTP, RTN, or RTZ; M is the exact largest finite value of format (ebits,sbits); E is that format's maximum unbiased exponent; U = 2^(E-sbits+1); and H = U/2.
